newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Labourites in pro-Palestinian state move.
newsitem.headline: Israel Labourites in pro-Palestinian state move.

text.p: Israel's main opposition Labour party took a step on Thursday toward tacit support for a Palestinian state, members of a party policy committee said.
But proposed changes to the party platform to give backing to Palestinian statehood were likely to meet weighty opposition from influential Labour centrists, Labour's secretary-general said.

Labour's political affairs committee passed on Thursday a proposal urging the party to change its platform such that Labour would "not rule out the establishment of a Palestinian state with limited sovereignty", committee members said.
Under the proposal, subject to approval by a party congress, the centre-left Labour would also recognise "the Palestinians' right to self-determination".
But Ehud Barak, an ex-army chief widely tipped to be the party's candidate for the premiership in elections scheduled for 2000, indicated he opposed the statehood proposal.

Last May, then-prime minister Shimon Peres of Labour was defeated by Benjamin Netanyahu of the hardline Likud, which struck chords with Israeli voters by charging Labour was moving too fast in granting concessions to PLO negotiating partners.
Likud campaigners said Labour policies would lead to a PLO-led Palestinian state, which they said would serve as a base for violent attacks on Israel.
Labour Secretary-General Nissim Zvili said on Thursday he believed the party congress would reject the proposal.
"I don't see room for the party changing its platform on the establishment of a Palestinian state," he told state television.
"We never believed an independent Palestinian state was the best solution, either for the Middle East or for Israel."
